taxonomyNote: NatureServe and Animal Diversity Web call this species Southern Watersnake (Nerodia fasciata); 'banded' is used for the nominate subspecies group, and salt-marsh populations formerly included are now N. clarkii.
fieldMarks: Dark stripe from the eye to the angle of the jaw.
Base colour gray, tan, dark olive or black, with dorsal cross bands along the entire body; belly off-white or white.

Nerodia f. fasciata has square dark ventral markings; N. f. confluens has wide bands (11-17 along the body) and reddish-brown rectangular belly-side spots; N. f. pictiventris has wavy reddish transverse lines on the belly.
Adults 61-106.7 cm; neonates about 24 cm and more vividly patterned than adults; females longer and heavier.
behavior: Active day and night; basks on banks and in edge vegetation, and is most active at night after summer rains.
Eats frogs, toads, salamanders, tadpoles, fishes and aquatic invertebrates; juveniles eat mostly fish, adults mainly frogs or large fish.
Hibernates beneath logs or rocks or in burrows; may leave an area in severe drought.
habitat: Vegetated freshwater ponds, lakes, marshes, wet prairies, sluggish streams and rivers, ditches and swamps; shelters in bank-side burrows or under debris.
Tolerates slightly brackish water (under about 1 ppt) but does not survive in saltwater.
range: Southeastern United States: eastern Texas, southeastern Oklahoma, Arkansas, Louisiana, southeastern Missouri, western Tennessee, Mississippi, southern Alabama and Georgia, Florida and the Coastal Plain of the Carolinas. Not in Canada.
